reden: Yes. The report’s “[Medium] eq/le/ge give false for equal values stored as M and as L” explicitly states that eq is a raw uint256 (bit-pattern) comparison, causing equal numeric values encoded with different mantissa sizes (M vs L, i.e., with the L flag set) to compare unequal. This matches H-04’s root cause (eq unwraps and compares packed words, ignoring the L_MANTISSA_FLAG), the same function (Float128.eq), same code path/mechanism, same attack scenario (two encodings of the same value), and would be fixed by normalizing/decoding before comparison as suggested. Severity labeling differences don’t matter; it’s the same vulnerability.
